items.evidence: gamerules.rs is the 26.3 snake_case table (keep_inventory, advance_time, spawn_mobs, max_block_modifications, ...); the /gamerule tree is built from it (vanilla.rs:301). Vanilla 1.21.7 rules are camelCase — javap on net.minecraft.world.level.GameRules: 56 rules (keepInventory, doFireTick, allowFireTicksAwayFromPlayer, ...). 220 corpus cases reject valid rules at cursor 9; 8 accept 26.3 names (keep_inventory). doFireTick is absent entirely (also pilot G4).
items.title: /gamerule rejects every 1.21.7 rule name; accepts 26.3 snake_case names

items.evidence: Top-level diff vs vanilla's tree.json (73 commands): Rust release tree adds /stopwatch, /swing, /fetchprofile, /unpublish, /compute, /posteffect (none in vanilla 1.21.7; corpus-proven for the first five), /time clock subcommands (pause, resume, rate, of <clock>, set <timemarker> — the timemarker node is why 'time set nope' parses; vanilla /time has only add/query/set), and /execute ... stopwatch. Dev-gated (raid, warden_spawn_tracker), Horizon-gated (pregen) and dedicated-only (ban, whitelist, ...) commands correctly excluded; tell/w redirects present; waypoint and dialog are in vanilla's tree (not defects).
items.method: command_parse triage + tree diff vs oracle tree.json
items.title: 26.x commands and subcommands in the 1.21.7 release tree

items.evidence: tree_world.rs:62 uses ResourceOrId("minecraft:worldgen/feature") (feature types). Vanilla PlaceCommand uses Registries.CONFIGURED_FEATURE (javap; placeFeature takes a ConfiguredFeature). minecraft:acacia is a configured feature (224 ids in the oracle registries), not a feature type — every /place feature <name> fails with no_such_element (22 cases). Fixture data is correct; the registry string is wrong.
items.title: /place feature looks up minecraft:worldgen/feature instead of configured_feature

items.evidence: vanilla.rs uses ArgType::Rotation for the trailing angle. Vanilla uses AngleArgument (single float) — javap: SetSpawnCommand and SetWorldSpawnCommand both call AngleArgument.angle()/getAngle(). Rust rejects a single value (rotation.incomplete, 8 cases) and accepts two values vanilla rejects (4 cases).
items.title: spawnpoint/setworldspawn parse the angle as a rotation (yaw+pitch)

items.evidence: tree_extra.rs: publish [<allowCommands>] [<port>]. Vanilla PublishCommand is publish [<allowCommands>] [<gamemode>] [<port>] (javap: BoolArgumentType, then GameModeArgument.gameMode, then IntegerArgumentType(0, 65535)). 'publish true survival' fails in Rust with parsing.int.expected (4 cases + follow-on cursor diffs).
items.title: /publish is missing the gamemode argument

items.evidence: (a) NBT components with an entity source are rejected when the selector string doesn't parse (component.rs nbt arm). Vanilla accepts {"nbt":"a","entity":"@x"}: EntityDataSource.compileSelector catches CommandSyntaxException and returns null (javap exception table). 4 OK-diff + 260 cursor-diff cases. (b) object components ({"object":"atlas"/"player"}) are accepted by Rust but rejected by vanilla — 1.21.7 has NO object component type (jar network/chat/contents/ holds only PlainText, Translatable, Keybind, Score, Selector, Nbt). 8 cases. The object arm is a 26.x carry-over.
items.title: Chat-component decoder: too strict on NBT sources, too lax on object components

items.evidence: (a) codec.rs dispatch() reads the "type" key, but loot item modifiers use the "function" key ({"function":"minecraft:set_count","count":1}) — every inline modifier fails with failed_to_parse (4 cases). (b) /item ... from entity <source> uses ENTITIES (multi) in tree_misc.rs; vanilla ItemCommands uses EntityArgument.entity() (single) for the source — 'Only one entity is allowed' (2 cases).
items.title: Item modifiers: inline JSON fails (wrong type key); multi-entity source accepted

items.evidence: args.rs particle_options: for minecraft:block, any non-string block_state is an error. Vanilla accepts the BlockState-codec SNBT form block_state:{Name:"minecraft:stone"} (2 cases). Rust requires a string or a compound with id; the Name-form compound is the form vanilla's codec takes.
items.title: Particle block_state compound with Name is rejected

items.evidence: (a) Duplicate-option errors roll back to the option-name start (selector.rs parse_options); vanilla reports at the end of the duplicated value (28 cases, e.g. @e[type=pig,type=cow]: vanilla cursor 34, Rust 30). (b) @a/@p/@r push minecraft:player into s.types but never mark type_option consumed, so can_use("type") stays true and @a[type=player] parses — vanilla rejects it as inapplicable (16 cases; Rust then fails later with a generic error).
items.title: Selector option errors: wrong cursor on duplicates; type= accepted for @a/@p/@r

items.evidence: tree_world.rs worldborder set/add time uses ArgType::Time (float + d/s/t suffix). Vanilla WorldBorderCommand uses IntegerArgumentType.integer(0) (javap: 4 call sites). Rust accepts 'worldborder set 100 10s' (2 cases) and suggests ["d","s","t"] after a complete time argument where vanilla suggests nothing (12 suggestion cases).
items.title: /worldborder time is a Time argument; vanilla uses an integer (seconds)

items.evidence: 'recipe give @s minecraft:stick': vanilla suggests nothing (start 0, end 0, empty list); Rust suggests prefix matches (minecraft:stick_from_bamboo_item, minecraft:sticky_piston) at the argument start (2 cases). Vanilla offers no completions once the last argument is complete and valid; Rust re-suggests.
items.title: Suggestions offered for complete valid arguments (recipe)

items.evidence: 'execute if items ... @@bad@@': vanilla "Unknown slot '@@bad@@'" at end of input; Rust reports an SNBT error mid-input (8 cases). 'item replace block ... <empty slot>': vanilla "Unknown slot ''"; Rust reports no_such_element one position later (2 cases). The slot-argument error path doesn't match vanilla's reporting.
items.title: Slot error text/cursor divergences

items.evidence: ARGUMENT_TYPES (horizon-protocol play/commands.rs) is 57 entries with count and order identical to vanilla 1.21.7's ArgumentTypeInfos registration order (javap static initializer) — the 481494bd fix holds. One entry carries the 26.x name: minecraft:team_color where vanilla's registry has minecraft:color (index 16). Functionally harmless for network decode (numeric ids; index 16 decodes to TeamColor either way), but a latent inconsistency for name-based comparisons.
items.title: Argument-type table carries the 26.x name at index 16 (team_color vs color)

items.evidence: The command_parse_fixture probe loads language only from the prepared-resources root (.local/horizon-client/1.21.7), which contains NO lang files, so lang::get(key) falls back to the key itself and every error renders as its translation key (command.unknown.command 55,949; command.unknown.argument 19,824; ...). The GAME is exonerated: it loads language from the pack root on the vanilla asset root (game/packs.rs startup_root), and the 1.21.7 client jar's en_us.json (7,392 keys) contains every key with exactly the vanilla text the oracle produced. Fix direction: load the fixture language from the vanilla asset root or resolve keys before comparing. Until fixed, the driver's error-text leg is unreadable.
items.title: command_parse fixture has no language data — 86,241 error-text mismatches are raw keys (probe defect, not a game defect)

systemic_note: The dominant defect pattern in this batch is 26.x carry-over into the 1.21.7 command surface: the gamerule table (B9-G01), the command tree (B9-G02), the object component type (B9-G06b), TeamColor (B9-O01), team_color (B9-G13) — the same bug class as the pilot's tag defects and the leakage audit's findings, in commands rather than tags. The other defects are local argument/type errors (wrong registry, wrong argument type, wrong key, wrong cursor). The 86,987 command_parse mismatches collapse to 13 game defects + 1 fixture defect; do not quote 86,987 as a defect count.
